title: Kestrel Commercial Fleet Lease Remarketing Fees and Terminal Rental Adjustment Shares
content:
# Remarketing Fee Table — Kestrel Commercial Fleet Lease

Kestrel's remarketing network sells turned-in and recovered units of the Kestrel Commercial Fleet Lease at auction. The table below is the per-unit remarketing fee and the business's share of a TRAC sale surplus over book value, by program tier.

| Program tier | Remarketing fee per unit sold (USD) | Share of a TRAC sale surplus over book value credited to the business |
|---|---|---|
| Kestrel Business Advantage | 395 | 90 percent |
| Kestrel Fleet Select | 395 | 90 percent |
| Kestrel Fleet Preferred | 350 | 95 percent |
| Kestrel Fleet Premier | 325 | 100 percent |
| Kestrel Fleet Enterprise | 295 | 100 percent |
| Kestrel National Fleet | 275 | 100 percent |

## Terms common to every tier

| Item | Every program tier |
|---|---|
| TRAC deficiency payment period | due 30 calendar days after the settlement invoice |
| Surplus applied first to other charges due on the master agreement | Yes |

## Reading the table

- The remarketing fee falls as the tier rises, from 395 in the two entry tiers to 275 in Kestrel National Fleet.
- The surplus share reaches the whole of the surplus (100 percent) from Kestrel Fleet Premier upward.
- **Hypothetical illustration.** Where a TRAC unit in Kestrel Fleet Preferred sells for net proceeds a hypothetical 1000 above its book value, the business's share is 95 percent of that excess, 950; in Kestrel Fleet Select the share of the same excess is 90 percent, 900.
